heroHeadline: USCIS Ends Automatic Deportation Protection for 200,000 Immigrant Children Effective Today; Senate $71.7B Enforcement Bill Heads to Floor Vote May 18
heroSubtitle: A USCIS policy change (PM-602-0198) took effect May 10, 2026, ending the automatic grant of deferred action and work authorization for approximately 200,000 Special Immigrant Juveniles — children adjudicated as abuse or abandonment victims by state courts — who remain in the EB-4 visa backlog awaiting green cards. The National Immigration Project of the National Lawyers Guild (NIPNLG) continues to challenge the reversal through A.C.R. v. Noem in the Eastern District of New York; USCIS issued the new April 10 memo specifically to moot a November 2025 court stay that had blocked an earlier June 2025 rescission. Immigration practitioners nationwide filed a surge of last-minute SIJ petitions before the May 8 (Friday) deadline. The Senate is scheduled to hold a floor vote on the $71.7 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package during the week of May 18 — ICE would receive approximately $38.2 billion alone, roughly 8× its FY2024 budget — as President Trump's June 1 signing deadline creates scheduling pressure; a CBO score published May 4 shows the Judiciary title alone would add $39.2 billion in outlays over 2026–2035. Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons remains in post until his May 31 resignation; no successor has been named. The D.C. Circuit unanimously blocked DHS's bid to enforce a 7-day notice rule for Congressional oversight visits to ICE detention facilities on May 8, preserving unannounced inspection rights. Judge Beryl Howell on May 8 barred ICE agents in D.C. from relying on a revised warrantless arrest memo she found legally deficient. The 11th Circuit struck down mandatory no-bond detention on May 6 — the second circuit to do so — creating a four-circuit split nearly certain to reach the Supreme Court. The Office of Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO) remains closed after its May 5 shutdown removed the sole independent watchdog from a detention system with 30+ FY2026 custody deaths at record pace.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, court records, and Congressional records
